question:
A retail chain manages data of quarterly stock in three stores (S1, S2, S3) for two products (A and B). The matrices for stock (in units) are:

Q1: $S = \begin{bmatrix} 350 & 420 \\ 400 & 385 \\ 370 & 415 \end{bmatrix}$

Q2: $T = \begin{bmatrix} 390 & 410 \\ 410 & 415 \\ 380 & 430 \end{bmatrix}$

(a) Find the total annual stock for each product in each store (add both quarters).

(b) If the price per unit is $p = \begin{bmatrix}250 \\ 300\end{bmatrix}$, find total inventory value for each store for the two quarters (matrix multiplication).

(c) For Q1, what is the difference in stock of Product A and B for each store?

(d) Create a new matrix representing the percentage increase in stock from Q1 to Q2 for each entry.

(e) Find the transpose of the percentage increase matrix and state one property of transpose used in your calculation.
explanation:
(a) Total annual stock:

$S + T = \begin{bmatrix}350+390 & 420+410 \\ 400+410 & 385+415 \\ 370+380 & 415+430 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}740 & 830 \\ 810 & 800 \\ 750 & 845\end{bmatrix}$

(b) Inventory value per store for each quarter:

For Q1: $S \times p = \begin{bmatrix}350 \times 250 + 420 \times 300 \\ 400 \times 250 + 385 \times 300 \\ 370 \times 250 + 415 \times 300\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}87,500 + 126,000 \\ 100,000 + 115,500 \\ 92,500 + 124,500\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}213,500 \\ 215,500 \\ 217,000\end{bmatrix}$

Repeat for $T$:

$T \times p = \begin{bmatrix}390 \times 250 + 410 \times 300 \\ 410 \times 250 + 415 \times 300 \\ 380 \times 250 + 430 \times 300\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}97,500 + 123,000 \\ 102,500 + 124,500 \\ 95,000 + 129,000\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}220,500 \\ 227,000 \\ 224,000\end{bmatrix}$

(c) Q1: $\begin{bmatrix}350-420 \\ 400-385 \\ 370-415\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}-70 \\ 15 \\ -45\end{bmatrix}$ (A minus B for each store)

(d) Percentage increase:

$\frac{T - S}{S} \times 100$

For (1,1): $\frac{390-350}{350}\times100 = \frac{40}{350}\times100 \approx 11.43$

For (1,2): $\frac{410-420}{420}\times100 = \frac{-10}{420}\times100 \approx -2.38$

For (2,1): $\frac{410-400}{400}\times100 = 2.5$

For (2,2): $\frac{415-385}{385}\times100 \approx 7.79$

For (3,1): $\frac{380-370}{370}\times100 \approx 2.70$

For (3,2): $\frac{430-415}{415}\times100 \approx 3.61$

So, matrix = $\begin{bmatrix}11.43 & -2.38 \\ 2.5 & 7.79 \\ 2.70 & 3.61\end{bmatrix}$

(e) Transpose:

$\begin{bmatrix}11.43 & -2.38 \\ 2.5 & 7.79 \\ 2.70 & 3.61\end{bmatrix}' = \begin{bmatrix}11.43 & 2.5 & 2.70 \\ -2.38 & 7.79 & 3.61\end{bmatrix}$

Property: $(A')' = A$ and $(A + B)' = A' + B'$

options.A:
(a) $S+T=\begin{bmatrix}740&830\\810&800\\750&845\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) Q1 value $=\begin{bmatrix}213500\\215500\\217000\end{bmatrix}$ and Q2 value $=\begin{bmatrix}220500\\227000\\224000\end{bmatrix}$.
(c) Q1 difference A minus B $=\begin{bmatrix}-70\\15\\-45\end{bmatrix}$.
(d) Percentage increase matrix $\approx\begin{bmatrix}11.43&-2.38\\2.50&7.79\\2.70&3.61\end{bmatrix}$.
(e) Transpose $\approx\begin{bmatrix}11.43&2.50&2.70\\-2.38&7.79&3.61\end{bmatrix}$; one property is $(A')'=A$.
options.B:
(a) $S-T=\begin{bmatrix}740&830\\810&800\\750&845\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) Q1 value $=\begin{bmatrix}220500\\227000\\224000\end{bmatrix}$.
(c) Difference $=\begin{bmatrix}70\\-15\\45\end{bmatrix}$.
(d) Percentage matrix is zero.
(e) Transpose is the same as the original matrix.
options.C:
(a) $S+T=\begin{bmatrix}40&-10\\10&30\\10&15\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) Matrix multiplication is not defined.
(c) Q1 difference $=\begin{bmatrix}350\\400\\370\end{bmatrix}$.
(d) Percentage increase matrix is $S+T$.
(e) Transpose is not defined.
options.D:
(a) $S+T=\begin{bmatrix}740&830\\810&800\\750&845\end{bmatrix}$.
(b) Q1 value $=\begin{bmatrix}213500&215500&217000\end{bmatrix}$.
(c) Difference $=\begin{bmatrix}-70&15&-45\end{bmatrix}$.
(d) Percentage increase matrix must be square.
(e) Transpose property does not apply.
